text:
For most reptile setups, look for a **portable power station with a pure-sine-wave AC outlet**, enough continuous wattage for your heater, and substantially more capacity (Wh) than you think you’ll need. Keep the reptile’s **thermostat in the circuit**—don’t run a heat source uncontrolled.

Capacity depends heavily on the heater and outage length. As a rough example, a 24 W heat mat plus the station’s own draw may use about 40 W, so a 288 Wh station might last **6–8 hours**, while a 2,073 Wh unit could last about **two days**. A 100 W ceramic emitter running at roughly half duty could use around 65 W including station draw, giving that larger unit about **a day**. Those are estimates, not measured runtimes. ([Dealectric’s reptile backup-power sizing guide](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))

So, as a starting point: **a few hundred Wh for a short outage and a roughly 2,000 Wh station for longer backup**—but check your heater’s actual wattage and allow extra capacity. If you share the heater wattage and how many hours you need, I can estimate a better size. For a short outage, insulating the enclosure and using safe emergency heat can also help; see [Petco’s outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage).
